transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-20
Start time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Rebecca (Orion Procurement), Evan (Orion Security), Nadia (Orion Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Kickoff to align on MSA/DPA redlines, liability cap, SOC2/KMS expectations, and pricing runway for a pilot.
- Redwood to deliver redlined MSA and short perf benchmark; customer to confirm residency and security checklist.

Topics: MSA liability and indemnity, DPA subprocessors & data residency, SLA targets (p95/p99 latency), pricing for pilot vs reserved capacity, KMS/HSM and SOC2 controls, onboarding timeline.

Action items (not exhaustive): Jordan to upload redlined MSA, Priya to run perf tests, customer legal to review DPA.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey thanks everyone for joining. I think we have a pretty full agenda, gonna run through contractual points first, then Priya will jump into performance and the pricing buckets. Rebecca, Evan, Nadia, can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Rebecca (Orion): Yes, loud and clear. Thanks Jordan.
[00:09] Evan (Orion): Yep good here.
[00:12] Nadia (Orion): All set.
[00:18] Jordan: Cool. So to kick off on the MSA and DPA, we've seen the initial redlines you sent, thanks for that. The two main asks we heard were: lower liability cap for enterprise pricing, and stronger data residency language. Is that still accurate?
[00:30] Rebecca: Yes that's correct. From procurement perspective the cap is the big blocker for finance. They want something that's more predictable. Also need clarity on subprocessors in the DPA, we have a pretty strict supplier list.
[00:40] Jordan: Understood. Priya, do you want to add anything on technical constraints that feed into the contract?
[00:44] Priya (Redwood): Sure. A couple things to flag — for Orion's expected latency SLOs we recommend either Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment. Hosted will work for small spikes but if you need region pinned files and KMS integration, you'll likely want the dedicated pool or Private with VPC. Also, note our KV cache behavior for chat workflows — sometimes folks call it K-V cash — it's basically prefix caching, impacts cost if you disable it.
[01:05] Evan: Sorry can you repeat the KV thing? We heard K-V cash haha.
[01:09] Priya: Yeah, sorry. KV cache — it's our key-value cache for transformer key/value states. If you enable prefix caching it reduces per-token compute for long chat sessions; if you disable it you pay more.
[01:20] Evan: Got it. From security, our big asks are: SOC2 type II evidence, explicit KMS/HSM integration and CMK support, and audit log retention for 12 months with export. Also we run periodic pen-tests and need a subprocessors list.
[01:34] Jordan: That's helpful. On SOC2 we are SOC2 Type II in our company docs; I will share the attestations. For KMS we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted has a bring-your-key option but with some limitations — we'll put the exact matrix in the doc.
[01:48] Nadia: On the DPA process, two items — control over subprocessors and a clear process for notification and opt-out. The current DPA language had a broad subprocessor clause. We'd like more explicit notice periods.
[01:59] Jordan: Makes sense. We can propose a 30-day notice and allow a right to object with remediation path; if not acceptable, fallback to remove data or transition plan — that's something legal can redline.
[02:12] Rebecca: For pricing, finance asked about a pilot rate vs committed reserved capacity. The spreadsheet you shared had hosted MSRP and a dedicated commit number, can you recap the delta?
[02:24] Priya: Sure. For hosted you pay usage per token with burstable throughput; cost is lower startup but variable as you scale. Dedicated is a monthly commitment for a GPU pool, predictability on p50/p95 throughput and lower per-token cost at scale. We usually see 20-40% unit cost savings at committed utilization.
[02:40] Rebecca: Are there minimum terms for dedicated? Our procurement generally wants a 3-month pilot or they push to annual commitments only.
[02:47] Jordan: We can do a 3-month proof-of-value (POV) on Dedicated with an opt-in to extend to annual. Pricing will reflect the shorter term but we can structure a pilot discount.
[02:58] Evan: Quick question about egress and data residency. If we pin to EU region, are tokens ever routed through US for fallback?
[03:06] Priya: Good question. We have smart routing: normally requests stay in-region. For failover we have policies — we can avoid cross-border fallback by restricting fallback tiers; that will be documented. But note some third-party monitoring endpoints might be multi-region unless we set a strict policy.
[03:23] Evan: Ok, need that in writing.
[03:25] Nadia: Back to liability, finance wants to cap liability at the greater of fees paid in last 12 months or a fixed $X. Would Redwood accept a cap tied to fees?
[03:36] Jordan: Our standard is a multiple of fees paid (usually 1x-3x depending on contract class). For enterprise deals we can negotiate down to 1x with certain carveouts removed. We need to understand your expected spend in the first year to line this up.
[03:50] Rebecca: For pilot we estimate $60k over 3 months, ballpark.
[03:55] Jordan: That's helpful. That would make the 1x cap roughly $60k which is low; we can discuss an alternative like a fixed $250k cap for the pilot or a tiered cap. We'll include options in the redline.
[04:06] Evan: Also need a warranty carveout for security incidents tied to third-party widgets — we cannot accept broad warranty that covers customer configs.
[04:14] Jordan: Agreed; our standard carveouts exclude customer misconfig and third-party code. We'll call that out.
[04:20] Nadia: On subprocessors, we also need a list of all infra providers and any subcontracted engineering teams that might access logs.
[04:28] Jordan: We'll provide a subprocessor list. For access to logs, we do have support engineers that can access production logs under controlled procedures — we can provide an approach and audit trail.
[04:38] Priya: FYI from ops side: if you want zero-support access then Private with on-prem would be the path; otherwise we provide role-based access and capture everything in our audit logs.
[04:48] Rebecca: What's the turnaround for providing SOC2 and subprocessor list? Procurement needs both to clear the vendor.
[04:53] Jordan: I can upload SOC2 report and the subprocessor list within 48 hours after the call.
[04:57] Rebecca: Great.
[05:00] Nadia: For the DPA we need language about breach notification windows — 72 hours is required for us. Is that standard?
[05:07] Jordan: We aim for 72-hour notification for incidents where we are the data processor; we can agree to that in DPA with clarifying language about investigative time.
[05:16] Rebecca: Next on SLA, can you confirm p95 and p99 latency numbers for the model families you plan to use? We're testing chat and summarization workloads.
[05:24] Priya: For the curated models we'd propose p95 sub-500ms for single-turn generation at short sequences on Dedicated, p99 under 1s in most cases, but it depends on sequence length and batching. For embedding workloads it's lower. I'll run a short benchmark using a representative chat sample and share the traces.
[05:41] Evan: Will you produce trace-level latencies and token counts? We need that for SRE signoff.
[05:45] Priya: Yes, I'll share traces, p50/p95/p99, and sample payloads.
[05:50] Rebecca: On pricing, can you send a cost model: pilot estimate, expected committed discount bands, overage terms?
[05:56] Jordan: Yes, we'll produce a pricing matrix with pilot, 6-month and annual options, plus overage rates.
[06:02] Nadia: A few legal clarifications: data deletion timeline after termination, return/erase certification, and a clause around data minimization.
[06:11] Jordan: We can commit to data deletion within 30 days of contract termination for hosted and dedicated; for Private/on-prem it's customer-controlled. We'll also provide a deletion certificate.
[06:21] Rebecca: Thanks. One more procurement ask — do you have an approval letter or financial references?
[06:26] Jordan: We can provide a reference list and a standard evidentiary packet — I'll include an org chart for support and billing as well.
[06:33] Evan: Quick technical note — if you plan to use quantized model variants for cost saving, we need to ensure they don't alter output fidelity for clinical use cases. Is there a QA path?
[06:45] Priya: Absolutely. For quantization profiles we'll provide evaluation sets and can run A/B tests with your prompts. If fidelity drop is material we won't recommend that profile for production.
[06:55] Rebecca: Great. Let's talk schedule. We need the redline and SOC2 within 48 hours, perf traces and pricing matrix by next Tuesday, and legal wants to meet again after they've had a chance to mark the DPA. Can we set a follow-up next Thursday?
[07:08] Jordan: Next Thursday works for us. I'll propose 14:00 UTC.
[07:12] Nadia: Works here.
[07:14] Rebecca: Confirmed.
[07:16] Jordan: Ok small wrap — I will: upload redlined MSA highlighting liability options, SOC2 attestation, subprocessor list within 48 hours. Priya will run a quick performance bench and share traces and a short writeup by 2026-04-27. Customer to confirm residency and any non-standard security controls by 2026-04-22. Legal to redline DPA and confirm subprocessors requirements by 2026-04-24.
[07:40] Evan: One last clarifying Q — encryption at rest: do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for hosted, or only for Dedicated/Private?
[07:47] Jordan: We support BYOK with limitations on hosted (works for encryption at rest but not for some ephemeral caches). For Dedicated and Private there is full CMK support and HSM integration for key rotation. We'll map that in the security matrix.
[07:58] Priya: I'll also include notes on backup retention windows and point-in-time restores — that was in the early security deck.
[08:04] Rebecca: Perfect. Anything else?
[08:06] Nadia: Nothing from legal.
[08:07] Jordan: Cool. We'll follow up with the artifacts. Thanks everyone.

Meeting end / recap:
- Recap: Redwood to deliver redlined MSA with liability options, SOC2 attestation, subprocessor list; Redwood SE to provide perf traces and SLA baseline; Orion to confirm residency and return redline to DPA.
- Next meeting: 2026-04-29 14:00 UTC (tentative) to review redlines and perf results.

Notes about transcript quality: auto transcript contained several misheard product names (e.g., \"K-V cash\" instead of \"KV cache\", \"Redwood Dedicate\" for Dedicated). Legal names occasionally concatenated; timestamps are approximate.
